MosoFin skill · duplicate-invoice-detection · learning guide

From one invoice number entered twice to the test the scan cannot run

This page shows how the skill finds a bill your business entered or paid twice, one level at a time. It starts with one invoice number that appears twice. It ends with the one rule that the scan cannot run from a MosoFin connection. The page quotes every rule from the skill itself. It also works every number in front of you.

The rules are the skill's ownThe page quotes each rule word for word, with the file and section it comes from.

How it thinks

Fourteen rules the whole skill runs on

Every level below applies one or more of these rules. The examples use one company, Northbrook Trading. The scan covers 1 July to 31 October, and September is the month under review. It reads 1,284 bills from 212 vendors, 1,197 bill payments and 14 open vendor credits. The sensitivity is Standard, and the Rule 3 window is 7 days.

Learning path

Six levels, from simple to complex

Check it yourself

Put in your own scan

Enter up to six clusters from your own scan, or load an example. For each cluster, pick the rule that matched, the amount per record, the record count and the paid status. Then pick the sensitivity. The page shows which clusters that setting puts in the headline and totals their exposure. It also counts the clusters below the setting. The page sends nothing anywhere.

Sensitivity
Clusters
ClusterRule matchedAmount per recordRecordsPaid status

The page counts one record in each cluster as the real bill. So the exposure of a cluster is the amount per record × (records − 1). The skill lists every cluster, and the sensitivity decides only the headline. Standard takes High and Very High. Strict adds Medium. Permissive takes Very High only. The other clusters count below the threshold. A credit cluster is never exposure. The page shows it as money owed to you, whatever the sensitivity. A Rule 7 cluster can occur only on the upload path, from uploaded supplier bank details. The "Northbrook, July to October" preset holds the six clusters from the levels. Under Standard: $1,250.00 + $4,860.00 + $3,200.00 = $9,310.00 in the headline, and 2 clusters below it: $980.00 + $950.00 = $1,930.00. Under Strict: $9,310.00 + $980.00 + $950.00 = $11,240.00.

Using it

What it asks, needs and gives back

Asks firstDo you want to use MosoFin, or upload the data yourself? Which company, and should the scan also run across your companies? Which period should the scan cover, and how far back before it? Which suppliers bill the same amount every month on purpose? Strict, Standard or Permissive, and what window for Rule 3? Do you have results from an earlier scan, with clusters already cleared? The method also asks for the Rule 8 threshold.
NeedsOn the upload path, the skill needs the AP register and payment history for the whole window. They give the vendor, invoice number, date, amount, payment date, payment method and status. It also needs the cheques, expenses and card charges by vendor, for Rule 9. The vendor master with inactive records, the open vendor credits and the open payables make the result better. Supplier bank details are optional, and they let Rule 7 run.
Gives backThe skill gives back seven sheets. They are a summary, the flagged clusters, the record detail, the vendor aliases to merge and the recovery plan. The last two are the rules-run sheet and a coverage sheet. Unpaid duplicates come first. Each flagged cluster shows its duplicate exposure and has columns for the reviewer's decision. The skill asks before it makes an Excel file.
NeverThe skill never voids a record, never merges a vendor and never asks a supplier for money. It never defaults the period or the entity. It never reports Rule 7 as finding nothing. It never saves bank details or a suspicion attached to a named person.
